# Attribution

The Lean proofs included in this **partial** formalization were jointly completed by **superpilot69 (X/Twitter: [@wofuhuola](https://x.com/wofuhuola)) and ChatGPT 6 Astra**. The human contributor selected the target, directed the project, reviewed scope and publication decisions, and is the submitting GitHub account. ChatGPT 6 Astra assisted with source analysis, proof development, Lean implementation, testing, and documentation.

This describes the collaboration on the submitted formalization. It does not claim a complete solution to JSP-000404 or original authorship of the classical mathematics.

Mathematical attribution:

- G. Szekeres, *On an extremum problem in the plane* (1941), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2307/2371290).
- P. Erdős and G. Szekeres, *On some extremum problems in elementary geometry* (1960/61), pp. 53–62, [original paper](https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1960-09.pdf). The direction-cover and binary-counting arguments follow this classical approach.
- B. Sendov, *Minimax of the angles in a plane configuration of points*, Acta Mathematica Hungarica 69 (1995), 27–46, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01874605), [public journal scan](https://real-j.mtak.hu/7467/).
- B. Kh. Sendov, *Compulsory configurations of points in the plane*, Fundamentalnaya i Prikladnaya Matematika 1:2 (1995), 491–516, [official paper record and full text](https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/fpm81).

This package's Lean source was written for this contribution using Mathlib. It does not copy another project's Erdős 504 Lean proof. Mathlib and its dependencies retain their own authorship and licenses; their source is fetched through the pinned Lake manifest and is not vendored here. Source papers are linked, not redistributed.

The new Lean source and verification script are provided under the accompanying [MIT license](LICENSE). Documentation follows the repository's CC BY 4.0 content license.
